reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the grant in p0030 runs only to Licensee, p0042/p0045 confine access to Licensee's own employees with any wider use requiring Licensor's discretionary consent (no notice-based affiliate path), assignment needs consent (p0149) and any Change of Control auto-terminates with deemed-reasonable refusal grounds (p0134) — this fails the fallback on both affiliate coverage and successor transferability, and Article IV's immediate termination for 'any breach' pushes it toward walk-away territory.

Redline is actionable and directionally right: it inserts Affiliates and contractors/introducing brokers acting on our behalf into the grant, deems 'employees of the Licensee' to include their personnel so the p0042/p0045 restrictions do not swallow the grant, adds consent-free successor assignment in an M&A transaction, and limits revocation to uncured material breach after 30 days' notice — i.e. it covers all three rule elements.

Changed-character ratio (0.47) is acceptable here because the rule requires adding new grant beneficiaries plus transfer and revocation language; the edit stays within the grant clause rather than rewriting unrelated text.

The failed 'no at-will revocation remains' check reflects that Article IV (p0049) and Article XX (p0134) still contain 'immediately terminate' upon any breach and Change-of-Control auto-termination. The inserted override sentence addresses this in substance, but we should also strike the immediate-termination sentence in Article IV and the auto-termination trigger in p0134 to avoid an internal conflict the Licensor could exploit.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the affiliate-on-written-notice fallback.
